key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 steel, delivering the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve boiler-steel oxidation protection through denser microstructures and protective oxide formation.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spray.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: After 50 cycles, bare steel showed intense oxide spalling and cracking, while the best coating showed 95.71% lower weight gain and protective oxide formation.
watch_item: Laboratory air-oxidation performance does not establish long-term durability under actual boiler combustion gases, deposits, or mechanical loading.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
